item.title: Are We Really on the Path to AGI?
item.dc:creator: Yuval Levin
item.description:
Sometimes, a curious amateur’s eye can discern tensions in the work of professionals that the intensity of their focused labor keeps them from seeing clearly themselves. Such amateurs point to questions more than answers, but innocent questions sometimes clear a path toward answers, too. This is the spirit in which what follows is put forward. This year, I’ve found myself a curious amateur working to engage with the enormously impressive conceptual and practical work that is pushing forward the development of artificial intelligence. item.title: ‘It’s a form of apocalypticism applied to science policy’
item.dc:creator: M. Anthony Mills, Ari Schulman
item.description:
Ari Schulman: Tony, I’ve spent the past year trying to make sense of what the Trump administration’s agenda is for science. It’s a tough job, because you hear two very different stories coming from the admin. One story is about restoring gold-standard science, restoring trust in science, solving the replication crisis, fueling cutting-edge research, and doing more to free scientists from needless grant paperwork and support them early in their careers. item.title: ‘To me it’s stupid to just indiscriminately cut science…. But it was also pretty stupid to just keep pouring money into science’
item.dc:creator: Daniel Sarewitz, Ari Schulman
item.description:
Ari Schulman: Dan, I’d like to start with a worry about science funding that goes back before the Trump era. item.title: The Pro-Human AI Declaration
item.dc:creator: The Future of Life Institute
item.description:
In March 2026, a coalition of interest groups and individuals, organized by the Future of Life Institute, issued the following declaration at HumanStatement.org. 1. Keeping Humans in Charge Human Control Is Non-Negotiable: Humanity must remain in control. Humans should choose how and whether to delegate decisions to AI systems. Meaningful Human Control: Humans should have authority and capacity to understand, guide, proscribe, and override AI systems. No Superintelligence Race: Development of superintelligence should be prohibited until there is broad scientific consensus that it can be done safely and controllably, and there is strong public buy-in. item.title: Is There Life on Mars, Pennsylvania?
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Snurenco
item.description:
SpaceX’s initial public offering of $1.8 trillion in June was the largest ever in history. Yet Mars, Elon Musk’s ambitious destination, is an airless desert whose median temperature of negative 80 degrees Fahrenheit makes it neither particularly warm nor inviting. Mars, Pennsylvania, however, is both — but nobody is bidding trillions to get there. Instead, people seem to want to leave. Going to Mars for a yoga class, or craft beer, or a tomato festival? All are available 20 miles north of Pittsburgh, where Mars has turned its planetary name into neighborly hospitality, local pride, and a joke everyone is invited...

item.title: Why I Do Not Have AC
item.dc:creator: Clare Coffey
item.description:
Every summer, at least once, the thermometer hits one hundred, the humidity breaks all previous records, and the message from the cosmos seems clear: you will give up and get air conditioning. Every summer, I resist. I do not eschew cooling technology for the sake of the climate, although you are welcome to tell people that if they ask. It is not the perverse need to prove that I could hack it, if suddenly dropped into various harrowing historical scenarios including but not limited to the Donner Party and the Vietnam War. item.title: Zoning Alone
item.dc:creator: Joseph Lawler
item.description:
Downtown commercial districts that empty out in the evenings, industrial areas far from population centers, family homes surrounded by nothing but other houses in developments with no nearby access to anything — no grocery stores or shops, no places of work or entertainment, no restaurants, day cares, or public parks: These are the distinguishing characteristics of the American urban form. If these are inconvenient, or ugly, or sad, why don’t property owners change them? The reason is that these features are a byproduct of property owners’ lack of property rights. item.title: Should Your Kids Be Born in a Pod?
item.dc:creator: Hannah Rowan
item.description:
Colossal Biosciences is going to bring back the woolly mammoth — if they can find a womb big enough to birth one. Their first solution is elephants. But surrogacy is too unreliable to produce mammoth calves at scale, so they’ve come up with Plan B: to create an artificial womb within the next year. It’s an ambitious goal. Scientists have been trying to develop artificial wombs since the 1950s for a wide array of medical purposes, especially improving survival rates for premature babies.
